newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Fletcher Energy reports production rise.
newsitem.headline: Fletcher Energy reports production rise.

text.p: Fletcher Energy Ltd on Monday reported total oil production for the June quarter of 13.7 million barrels of oil equivalent (mmboe), up 22 percent on the corresponding quarter of the 1995/96 year.
Production for the year ended June 30 was a record of 50.3 mmboe, up 21 percent on the previous year.

The company said production of liquids rose 61 percent to 5.6 million barrels for the quarter, reflecting increased condensate production from the Maui field and the inclusion of three months of oil production from the Maui F and D sands.
Gas production at 46.9 billion cubic feet (bcf), rose by nine percent as demand from New Zealand users, particularly thermal power stations, was maintained at high levels.
In Canada, oil and gas production was up 12 and eight percent respectively on the corresponding quarter of the previous year.
Onshore New Zealand the Piakau-1 exploration well was brought on to production and the Mangahewa-2 appraisal well was successfully fractured.
As at July 28, Fletcher Energy had six million barrels of Tapis swaps at a weighted average price of US$19.89 per barrel maturing over the remainder of the 1997/98 financial year.
For the 1998/99 year it has 125,000 barrels of Tapis swaps at an average weighted price of US$19.94.
